recommendation: Keep the fixed commit as-is. It implements the final Jira decision in current build inputs and removes the remaining implementer-facing contradiction without broadening Period semantics beyond the approved correction.
issue_request: FHIR-38819 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for the R5 datatype page. It requested replacing the Period.end Meaning if Missing statement that a missing end means the period is ongoing with wording that no end date/time was known or planned at instance creation.
initial_application: No prior source-history commit mentioning FHIR-38819 was found. The earlier FHIR-16979 implementation changed the Period.end definition in source/datatypes/period.xml, but the Period.end missing-meaning cell and datatype narrative still said or implied that absence meant ongoing.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini maps datatype pages to datatypes.html, and source/datatypes/period.xml is the authoritative spreadsheet source for the Period datatype. FHIR-I Methodology/Data Types minutes for 2023-02-15 record the FHIR-38819 persuasive-with-modification vote. A 2022 Zulip thread independently identified the same contradiction, and no conflicting later community or Jira decision was found.
reconciliation: Changed source/datatypes/period.xml to use the approved missing-meaning wording and updated the Period.end short description so it no longer implies that a missing end is equivalent to ongoing. Updated source/datatypes.html to align the narrative while preserving guidance for explicit planned future end dates.
source_changes: source/datatypes/period.xml: updated Period.end Meaning if Missing to the approved no-known-or-planned-end wording and changed the short description from 'if not ongoing' to 'if known'.
source/datatypes.html: aligned the Period narrative with the same missing-end rule and clarified that known or planned future ends should be represented explicitly.
